articles.title: 5 takeaways from Broncos' overtime win vs. Seahawks on 'TNF'
articles.summary: Here are five quick takeaways from the Broncos' win over the Seahawks on Thursday night.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos barely hung on to defeat the Seattle Seahawks in a 17-14 overtime victory on Thursday Night Football last night. Here are five quick takeaways coming out of that ugly win.

1. Denver's defense dominated : The Broncos ' defense carried the team, especially in the second half. Vance Joseph's unit ended the night with 17 quarterback hits, nine pass breakups, five sacks, two interceptions and a forced (and recovered) fumble. Seven different defenders recorded at least a half sack as the unit harassed Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold throughout the contest.

2. Luke Wattenberg's snaps are becoming a serious problem : Wattenberg's snap delivery has been extremely erratic, and if it's not corrected (or if Wattenberg isn't replaced), it will eventually cost the Broncos. One of Wattenberg's bad snaps killed a drive on Thursday. If the trend of bad snaps continues, it could directly lead to a turnover, or even a loss.

3. Broncos' backup cornerbacks stepped up : Pat Surtain ( ankle ) remained sidelined and Riley Moss ( ribs ) was limited, leaving Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine to step up once again. Jaxon Smith-Njigba heated up in the fourth quarter, ending the game with 12 receptions for 134 yards, but Denver held him out of the end zone and limited Seattle's offense to just one touchdown overall. KAD secured an interception and slot cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian essentially sealed the win with an overtime interception. The Broncos have incredible depth at cornerback.

4. Bo Nix was bad, and Denver's offense struggled : After taking a 14-3 lead into halftime, the Broncos' offense had six straight punts and then a kneel-down in the second half before OT. Nix completed 17 of his 27 passes (63%) for 107 yards with no scores (and fortunately, no turnovers). Believe it or not, his performance arguably looked worse than those pitiful numbers suggest. Nix appeared afraid to run and made several poor decisions late in the game that nearly cost a win. It seems that the third-year quarterback is either in his head ( perhaps because of his ankle ), or he has significantly regressed. Either option is very concerning for the team's long-term outlook.

5. Broncos have a much-needed mini bye to recover : Jaylen Waddle briefly left the game with a shoulder injury , Tyler Badie injured his thumb and did not return and Jonah Elliss was carted off the field late in the fourth. Surtain and safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ) also remain sidelined. Fortunately, Denver now has a mini bye to potentially help some of those players recover. After playing on TNF , the Broncos will have 10 days until they play again on Oct. 25.

Up next on Denver's schedule is a road game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7.

articles.title: Seahawks continue fumbling at an alarming rate in TNF loss
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks continued fumbling the football at an alarming rate in their TNF loss to the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks lost another nailbiter in Week 6 . They were defeated 17-14 by the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football in overtime. For a third consecutive defeat, losing the turnover battle was decisive to Seattle's loss.

The Seahawks have committed a minimum of three turnovers throughout each of their three defeats. They've totaled 10 turnovers in three losses. Quarterback Sam Darnold threw two interceptions versus the Broncos, meaning he's thrown 7 INTs in just four complete games.

Seahawks wide receiver/kick returner Rashid Shaheed lost a fumble against the Broncos. The Seahawks were down 14-3 when Shaheed fumbled an end-around in Broncos territory (30-yard line). It was the perfect microcosm to represent this struggling offense right now.

The Seahawks have lost five fumbles in six games. Granted, they've already played in Week 6, but only two NFL teams enter the weekend having lost more fumbles than the Seahawks have. In total, Brian Fleury's struggling offense has committed 12 turnovers. Only the winless Los Angeles Chargers have more giveaways (13) on offense.

Darnold is now tied for the league-lead with Drake Maye and Justin Herbert in interceptions (7). He's played fewer games than they have. Shaheed, George Holani, Emanuel Wilson, and Jadarian Price have lost fumbles for the Seahawks this season. This offense just can't do anything right.

articles.title: Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas vs. Florida Gators
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns try to bounce back after a tough loss in Red River against the Florida Gators. Our staff gives their predictions for the game.
articles.body:
It seems fitting that Halloween is around the corner, because the Texas Longhorns have a lot of demons to exorcise. The Longhorns are coming off one of the programs worst losses in years . And the Florida Gators are a huge reason Texas missed last year's College Football Playoff .

Texas' second half collapse in the Red River Shootout last weekend has reverberated throughout college football. Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning has been a punching bag for the national media and UT haters around the nation. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian hasn't fared much better.

Manning threw two catastrophic fourth quarter interceptions last Saturday against Oklahoma that has made everyone question whether he's even on the right track. And Sark's play-calling has come heavy criticism.

It is almost a carbon copy of the reaction last year after the loss to Florida. If the Longhorns are going to start a redemption tour that sweeps UT into the CFP, the Gators are a good opponent to start against.

Florida set the college football world on fire after upsetting Ole Miss three weeks ago. But back-to-back losses have seen the Gators come crashing back down to earth.

For Texas to keep their CFP hopes alive, this is a pseudo must-win. Florida comes with a dangerous but struggling offenses as of late. The defense is where Texas could earn a major advantage. The Gators defense has struggled mightily all season, especially defending the pass.

This should be a game where Manning and the Texas offense can find a rhythm early and often. I expect Texas to begin making offensive adjustments, slow down Jadan Baugh and get the Longhorns a rather comfortable win this weekend.

I think Texas wins big. The offense will click better than it has all season. Manning will look the best he has all season and the offense puts some points on the board.

Defensively, Texas has another big day. Florida QB Aaron Philo is questionable, as are WRs Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton. The Gators will get some yards on the ground with super running back Jadan Baugh. But the passing game will be a mess.

If Texas is (still) a title contender, they need to use this game as a springboard for the rest of the season.

articles.title: Barcelona face staff strike ahead of El Clasico as Camp Nou workers demand pay rise and more employees
articles.summary: Barcelona are facing a potential disruption to operations surrounding the Clasico against Real Madrid on October 25, with a group representing the club’s per...
articles.body:
Barcelona are facing a potential disruption to operations surrounding the Clasico against Real Madrid on October 25, with a group representing the club's permanent seasonal workers announcing a three-day strike over what they describe as deteriorating working conditions.

According to SPORT , the industrial action will begin at midnight on October 23 and continue until 06:00 on October 26, covering the period of one of the biggest fixtures on Barcelona's calendar.

The workers cite staff shortages, alleged contractual irregularities and a lack of concrete commitments from the club among their main grievances.

Barcelona, however, insist that the strike will not jeopardise the staging of the Clasico or other sporting events scheduled during the period.

Why Barcelona's seasonal workers are striking

The strike committee has accused the club of allowing working conditions to deteriorate, pointing to "the failure to honour agreements, contractual irregularities, and instances of discrimination between male and female staff at the same club."

The group has also raised concerns about services being outsourced to external companies, arguing that the situation is affecting the quality of services provided to members and supporters.

Barcelona are facing workers' strike ahead of El Clasico. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"We warn that this situation is undermining service standards, reducing the ability to respond to incidents and harming the service provided to members and supporters.

"We consider this industrial action to be a last resort in the face of a lack of progress and concrete commitments," the strike committee said in a statement.

The workers are demanding a pay rise and a 50% increase in their numbers, which would take the workforce from approximately 60 to 90 employees.

Clasico is among several Barcelona events affected

The industrial action will extend beyond the men's first-team meeting with Real Madrid at Spotify Camp Nou.

According to SPORT, it will also affect all facilities where the workers carry out their duties, including the Johan Cruyff Stadium, the Palau Blaugrana and the Joan Gamper Training Centre.

Consequently, Barcelona's women's first-team matches, basketball and handball fixtures, and youth-team activities could also be affected during the strike period.

Barcelona have a decision to make (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

As such, the Clasico is expected to face particular operational pressure because of the scale of the event.

Barcelona estimate that a match of this magnitude involves around 80,000 people, including spectators and security personnel deployed around the stadium.

Barcelona insist Real Madrid match will go ahead

Despite the workers' concerns, Barcelona maintain that they have sufficient organisational capacity to manage any potential incidents and ensure that matches proceed normally.

The club has also emphasised that the group consists of around 60 permanent seasonal workers operating under their own collective agreement, with pay conditions that it says exceed the sector's usual standards.

Barcelona insist they respect the employees' demands and will continue negotiations.

However, with the strike scheduled to overlap with the Real Madrid fixture, the outcome of those discussions will be important in determining how the club manages operations throughout the busy period.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca reveals Pep Guardiola meeting after Man City defeat to PSG: ‘It’ll always be his house’
articles.summary: The Premier League leaders aim to bounce back after a blow in the Champions League at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain, with Maresca sharing his views on the...
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca has revealed how he met Pep Guardiola following Manchester City 's defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League midweek.

The City boss met with his predecessor at the Etihad Stadium after the game, with Guardiola present to show support following the bombshell guilty verdict from the independent commission on the 115 charges.

But the Italian has shared how Guardiola met him following the setback at the hands of the two-time defending European champions.

"I saw him after the game," Maresca said. "Not before, we were talking about the game, the first half, the second half, he was very happy to be at the stadium.

"Very positive about things he's seen in the game. It was great for the fans to see him at the stadium. It'll always be his house."

Maresca is also content with how the club has handled the damaging news in recent weeks and added that his trust towards the club remains at "100 per cent".

"We handled it quite good, the fans, the team, everyone, tomorrow is three points game, the same as Anfield away, it's important to continue the run and try to win," Maresca added.

"I'm very happy, I said many times, I don't feel any kind of stress about the outside situation, it's something I don't control. I focus on how to win the next games.

"It's very dangerous, they have the whole week to prepare. It'll be very tough, for us it's important, a great opportunity to win and go six points clear.

"I'm quite respectful person, everyone can say what they want and agree with what they want. From my point of view, the wise way is to wait for the final word. People want to speak about this situation. I completely trust the club, I don't need people outside of the club to understand the situation. It's very clear, I trust the club, 100 per cent.

During City's 3-0 win at Liverpool last week, fans in the away section of Anfield celebrated with blow-up bananas in a nod to the club's past in the lower divisions, with Maresca keen to experience the gesture once more against Ipswich at the weekend.

"It was very nice," Maresca admitted. "I didn't know the history about the bananas, I hope to see many bananas in the stadium.

"It creates a nice envuroin for the fans and everyone in the stadium. I have four kids, they already asked me, tomorrow they will be in the stadium and ask me.

articles.title: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick says squad not affected by Lisandro Martinez fallout
articles.summary: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick says he is telling the truth about the club moving on from Lisandro Martinez's explosive post-match interview.
articles.body:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says he is "telling the truth" when he says the club have moved on from Lisandro Martinez's explosive post-match comments this week.

Carrick's close friend and team-mate Wayne Rooney led the condemnation of Martinez, saying the Argentine defender could "rip the dressing room apart" with his attack on United's hierarchy after the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Former United skippers Roy Keane and Gary Neville have also had their say, among a huge amount of analysis.

Martinez has apologised for the timing of comments, which turned the spotlight on director of football Jason Wilcox, but not for the words themselves.

"There's a lot of people who say a lot of things - ex-pros or not ex-pros - it doesn't necessarily mean they understand what is going on here," said Carrick in his pre-match media conference at United's Carrington training ground.

"Just because people talk on the outside doesn't mean that is the truth. I am telling you the truth. The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I have seen it for a while. That is it, plain and simple. We are living it every day and know what it feels like.

"We are emotional and care a lot. Sometimes someone says something that maybe you shouldn't say at that certain time, but it doesn't distract us from what we are creating here and the environment and spirit within the group.

"It [the squad] is not affected, I am telling you."

Carrick confirmed Martinez would be "part of the squad" for Sunday's Premier League trip to Leeds at Elland Road (14:00 BST).

Martinez apologises for outburst and fined by Man Utd

Man Utd a circus after Martinez comments - Keane

Wilcox the target again in another damaging Man Utd fallout

We're in it together - Carrick deflects Wilcox criticism

Martinez singled out the 'technical director' for criticism in Madrid.

There was no mention of Wilcox in his statement, although the former Leeds and Blackburn player, who was made United's director of football in the aftermath of Dan Ashworth's sacking in December 2024, was part of the discussions with Martinez that led to his latest statement on his conduct.

Wilcox is back in the spotlight, after also being targeted by Ruben Amorim in his final press conference before his dismissal in January.

The 55-year-old has only spoken publicly once since, to United's own media channel, 12 months ago.

"I don't think it's for me to say whether he should or not," said Carrick, when asked if Wilcox should be the one explaining his actions to the media.

"I've got no problem sitting here, talking to you guys and leading the group, leading the team, leading the football club from this position. We're all in it together.

Carrick does not feel Martinez's failure to mention Wilcox by name is an issue.

"He's released his statement, he's realised he's made a mistake, and I think that's enough for all of us to move on with," he said.

"We ask for passion, we ask for emotion, we ask for fire and we ask for players to care. There's a way of doing that, and that's already been acknowledged.

"But we need to carry that intensity, that willingness, togetherness and spirit and everything else you can bring with that. As a group, we need to use it, and we've got to use it in the right way."

Not about me - under-pressure Carrick faces up to Leeds trip

The negative headlines are the last thing Carrick needed at the present time.

His side go to Leeds on the back of a five-match winless run. United have not gone six games without a victory since the end of the 2018-19 campaign, just after Ole Gunnar Solskjaer had been confirmed as permanent manager.

Carrick knows the importance of ending that sequence in terms of easing the pressure on his own future.

However, he refuses to accept that as being crucial.

"I don't need results," he said. "We all need results.

"It's not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual. It is bigger than me, bigger than any player, or anyone else who works at this football club. It always has been.

"I don't go into every day at work in this situation, [ahead of] this game, thinking it's about me. It's really not. It's about the football club; what we stand for, what we live for, the history, the things that we need to live up to. That's what drives us."

Martinez's outburst was triggered by United's lengthy injury list that led to Ayden Heaven playing at left-back in Madrid.

Cover for Luke Shaw, who missed the game through injury, and Benjamin Sesko were viewed by some as being crucial in the summer.

In addition to Shaw's absence, Sesko is yet to start a Premier League game this season.

The Slovenia forward, a £74m signing from RB Leipzig in August 2025, suffered a recurrence of the shin injury that curtailed his 2025-26 season in last month's EFL Cup defeat by Brighton.

For the third pre-match press conference running, Carrick said he was unable to give a timescale on Sesko's return.

"Ben's kind of still undergoing a couple of checks before we update on timelines," he said.

"We're just trying to be clear with what that looks like but he's still a little bit further away."

Mucha referencia a «fuentes del club», pero muy poca distancia respecto de lo que esas fuentes quieren colocar. Pareces un lorito, pero con teclado. Y para que no se confundan los protagonistas: ese alto ejecutivo cuyas expresiones reproduces NO es el mismo que llama a las redacciones de los medios pidiendo ceses de periodistas y presiona para que se aparte a ejecutivos de empresas. Son personas distintas. Y esas llamadas y esas presiones no son una historia del pasado. Son presente. La dirección del Real Madrid dirige una orquesta de portaCOCES y Real Madrid TV lleva la voz cantante. Su partitura es siempre la misma: seleccionar las jugadas que interesan, repetir el agravio, alimentar la sospecha y señalar a los enemigos. Ese método recuerda a mecanismos de propaganda que explotó Goebbels, ministro de Propaganda de la Alemania nazi: repetición sistemática, construcción de un enemigo y subordinación de los hechos al relato. La comparación es con esas técnicas de propaganda, no con una ideología ni, por supuesto, con la afición madridista. Real Madrid TV es una pieza central de esa maquinaria. ¿Dónde está el análisis completo de los partidos de cada jornada? ¿Dónde están los posibles errores que perjudican a otros clubes o los que favorecen al Real Madrid? Si aplicaran a todos los encuentros la misma lupa, quizá el resultado les estropearía el guion. Pero el guion exige que el Real Madrid aparezca siempre como víctima. Y así se llega al extremo de presentar incluso el NO ERROR como error y de utilizar el caso Negreira como explicación permanente de cualquier decisión que no les guste. La sospecha se da por demostrada y la conclusión está escrita antes de que empiece el partido. Y esa misma técnica se traslada ahora a los horarios: se cuenta lo que alimenta el agravio y se oculta el contexto que permitiría comprobarlo. Pues hablemos de horarios, Tomás. Que ese alto ejecutivo que alimenta a los portaCOCES explique cuántas peticiones de cambio de horario y de día ha presentado el Real Madrid y cuántas se han atendido.(En este tema va el primero de la clasificación). Las aceptadas también. Que no cuente únicamente la que le interesa para construir la polémica de turno. Y que incluya las peticiones relacionadas con el calendario para facilitar la celebración de los eventos que la "super licencia" permite realizar en el Santiago Bernabéu. Porque para solicitar que se acomode la competición a sus necesidades tienen mucha iniciativa; para reconocer las solicitudes atendidas, bastante menos memoria. Ese es el balance que hay que publicar: qué pidió el Real Madrid, qué se le concedió y qué no pudo atenderse, con sus motivos. Los horarios afectan también al rival, a otros clubes, a los aficionados y a los compromisos audiovisuales de la competición. Una petición no se convierte en un derecho porque proceda del Real Madrid, ni una negativa demuestra una persecución. Laliga defiende a su competición. Lo que no resulta serio es pedir ajustes de días, horarios y calendario y, después, presentar cada desacuerdo como una prueba de que LaLiga perjudica al club. Si se quiere hablar de trato recibido, se cuenta TODO el trato recibido. Tomás, ahí tienes preguntas concretas para tus fuentes. Y Real Madrid TV tiene material para un programa: las solicitudes del club y las respuestas que ha recibido. Veremos si dedican a ese historial el mismo entusiasmo que a los vídeos de agravios. Después, los demás portaCOCES amplifican el mensaje. Real Madrid TV pone las imágenes, otros ponen los titulares y todos repiten la misma acusación.

articles.title: Luis García Plaza, de los elogios a Mourinho a las quejas arbitrales
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Sevilla ensalza la figura del portugués y repasa las decisiones por las que se sintió perjudicado en el Ciutat de València
articles.summary: El entrenador del Sevilla ensalza la figura del portugués y repasa las decisiones por las que se sintió perjudicado en el Ciutat de València
articles.body: En la previa del duelo de este domingo entre el Real Madrid y el Sevilla, Luis García Plaza no escatimó en lanzar elogios hacia José Mourinho, con quien aseguró que mantiene una buena relación desde hace años: "Su currículum habla por sí solo. El otro día va a Roma y la gente local canta su nombre y le saca una pancarta. Es uno de los mejores entrenadores del mundo ahora y desde hace años. Llevamos mucho tiempo enfrentándonos y tengo muy buena relación con él. Espero saludarlo como siempre y hablar un poquito de fútbol, que siempre charlamos. Es un tío que le mete mucho carácter a los equipos, compiten mucho y van a full, y creo que se nota en este Madrid. El otro día la remontada viene un poco de su carácter". García Plaza quiso ser comprensivo con el estamento arbitral, pero no esquivó la crítica. "Los árbitros nos han dicho que podemos expresar cualquier opinión sobre una jugada sin faltar al respeto. No valoro absolutamente nada de Vinícius, como la semana que viene no lo haré con Osasuna. Cuando es el Madrid me preguntáis, estoy acostumbrado, pero no valoro jugadas de nadie. Todavía no me han preguntado por una jugada del partido del Levante por la que a Miguel Sierra tienen que operarle y no pitaron ni falta. En todos los equipos sentimos cosas así. Todos somos humanos, yo me equivoco muchas veces", admitió. En cuanto al último encuentro ante el Levante, Luis García Plaza comentó varios episodios que han generado molestia en el cuadro hispalense: "Llevamos 70 minutos de descuento en ocho partidos cada vez que vamos ganando, menos el día del Rayo que íbamos empate. Desde el máximo respeto y la máxima humildad, el otro día nos sentimos perjudicados: la expulsión de Isaac, la acción en que se lesionó gravemente Miguel y esa jugada en la que hubo un error del cuarto árbitro al dejar entrar a un jugador y le sacan la amarilla a Castrín, que estuvo condicionado toda la segunda parte". Para finalizar, técnico madrileño respondió sobre cómo aislar mentalmente a la plantilla respecto a la presión mediática que rodea a los arbitrajes. "No comento nada de lo que hace el Real Madrid con su televisión, es su decisión. Yo hablo por mí y los árbitros siempre van a encontrar un entrenador que intente ayudarles, pero que también en un momento se centre en lo futbolístico. Jugamos 11 contra 11, ellos son muy buenos y vamos a ver si somos capaces de superarlos", concluyó.

articles.title: Chelsea: Jordan Henderson and Moises Caicedo starred in midfield against Bournemouth and will be key after Reece James injury blow
articles.summary: Jordan Henderson was player of the match last Saturday and Moises Caicedo shone on his return to the Chelsea XI; manager Xabi Alonso has been searching for a solution in midfield and, with Reece James out injured, the Henderson-Caicedo combination could be the answer for the Blues
articles.body:
Chelsea have made an erratic start under the Spaniard but last Saturday the midfield partnership of Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson brought control and balance to the team in a 5-1 thrashing of Bournemouth.

"For me, it's fundamental that we get that area strong," Alonso told the media after that game, well aware of how Chelsea's excellent attacking play in the early weeks of the season has been undermined by a leaky defence, exposed in end-to-end contests.

The answer lies in the middle of the pitch.

Alonso, a star central midfielder himself during his playing days, has used a variety of players and combinations in that area through his first six Premier League games.

Reece James has been a regular selection. But the Chelsea captain's knee surgery, which is going to keep him out for the coming months , necessitates Alonso settling on a different option.

The Caicedo-Henderson combination could be the partnership he takes forward, with Everton away up next. They showed their character and quality last time out.

Caicedo's return to fitness was always going to be a key element to the solution. The Ecuadorian had been limited to just 14 minutes of football this season before playing 72 against Bournemouth.

His impact on the team was clear at Stamford Bridge. He topped the tackles won and interceptions metric for Chelsea, and also used the ball efficiently, posting a 96.4 percent passing accuracy, the best of any starter from either side.

"With him, we have a better midfield area," said Alonso plainly.

"When you are better in the middle, you have a more complete team, and I think that is something to build around.

"He's going to be a key player for us. We knew that, and we have seen today."

But if Caicedo delivered his expected attributes, Henderson delivered a couple of sensational surprises, whipping in two brilliant long-range goals. His influence with his all-round game - at 36 years of age - may be an even bigger surprise to his critics.

The former Liverpool captain's controversial switch to Al Ettifaq in 2023 and subsequent struggles at Ajax seemed to be spelling the end to his career. But after Brentford brought him back to these shores, England boss Thomas Tuchel saw the situation differently, taking Henderson to the World Cup.

Now Alonso is giving him an even more prominent role.

"We signed him for everything - if he's able to score two beauties, as today, we are more than happy for him," smiled Alonso when asked about the player of the match.

Henderson was everywhere against Bournemouth. He covered 11.9km, the most of any player, despite setting the record for being the oldest Chelsea player to be directly involved in three goals in a Premier League game.

"Apart from the goals, he's done many, many good things," said Alonso.

"A very 'midfielder' performance, always being involved in the action, always giving solutions to the team-mates."

The wider impact was crucial. Alonso described Chelsea's display as "a very complete performance" and said Henderson and Caicedo bring the best out of players around them.

"Both, in terms of qualities, are different, in terms of the positioning as well. I think that they help each other well," said Alonso.

"And they give presence, they give stability. You know that they are going to be the ones that are going to be helping the rest, not just for his qualities, because they understand the game, they can play in shorter spaces, but as well, defensively, they give good balance."

Alonso made a point of referencing Romeo Lavia and Valentin Barco in his post-match assessment last Saturday and he did the same in his pre-Everton press conference on Friday. They are two players who have also been deployed in central midfield this term.

Squad depth is going to be important, even if Chelsea are not involved in Europe this season. But the Caicedo-Henderson axis could be his winning formula.

Everton away on Saturday will be the next test to see if the pair can continue to bring cohesion and control to Alonso's Chelsea.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta says Arsenal plan to take another team photo including William Saliba after defender's omission
articles.summary: William Saliba was left out of Arsenal's team photograph for the 2026/27 season earlier this week; Mikel Arteta explained it was taken because of commercial obligations despite defender's absence; club will retake image
articles.body:
Arsenal supporters were left baffled by Saliba's omission from the official 2026/27 picture as the club revealed he was unavailable to attend due to a medical appointment.

Saliba is yet to play this season because of a back injury but the 25-year-old remains a key player, having made 184 appearances for the club, which heightened the intrigue around his omission.

"What happened was that we have tried to do that picture three times already and we had to cancel it last minute for different reasons," explained Arteta ahead of Arsenal's away trip to Nottingham Forest, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

"We had some commercial obligations, we had some people who flew over to do that, so we decided to do that picture.

"We will have another picture with the whole family.

"Hopefully we can get them all together at some point one day, and we'll announce that as well."

Arteta replied "yes" when asked to confirm that Arsenal planned to retake the picture and insisted Saliba was "completely fine" about the situation.

He said: "Well, it wasn't in his hands. But Willy is normally happy about everything. He knows how loved he is. He was taking some banter from the players and he is completely fine."

Saliba resumed training on the grass earlier this month and Arteta added that he is progressing positively, with a scan scheduled for next week as he edges closer to a return to action.

"I think next week we have another MRI with him to see how the healing process is going," he said.

"But every sign so far has been very, very positive. It will be good to have him."

Arteta added that Martin Zubimendi is in contention to return against Forest after injuring himself in the warm-down following the Leeds game along with Piero Hincapie , who will be out for another one or two weeks.

Christos Tzolis , meanwhile, underwent an MRI scan on Thursday to assess his recovery from the hamstring injury he suffered on international duty with Greece.

"It's progressing really well," Arteta added of the winger. "Another one that hopefully we can have back in a few weeks."

Arteta 'far from happy' about photo gaffe

Sky Sports News reporter Gary Cotterill at Arsenal's training ground:

When it comes to facing tricky questions, Mikel Arteta has things easier right now than his counterparts on both sides of Manchester, but it's not all plain sailing at Arsenal.

In a week of warm-down injuries, incomplete team photos and job-cut announcements, the Arsenal manager knew there would be some tricky issues to deal with.

As if that wasn't enough, the off-field issues continued as the tough questions started.

A few minutes into the news conference the microphone under Mikel's mouth stopped working.

It meant his answer underlining that Arsenal are no longer the set piece kings - 20 of their 21 goals so far this season have come from open play - had to be repeated.

This time "with all the family included".

It will be retaken after Saliba was left out of the line-up published this week.

Arteta went into detail about how it happened. But is clearly mystified as to why it happened. And, I understand, far from happy about it behind the scenes.

Nevertheless he spoke with good humour and a smile on his face, saying Saliba was fine about what happened.

Arteta's demeanour was very different, of course. when it came to my inevitable question about the Arsenal "restructuring" announced this week. Sixty jobs will go around the club.

He made the point twice that he's not the person to answer such questions, but he gave an answer anyway, saying such decisions have to be taken so the club can evolve and achieve its aims.

articles.title: Avalancha Roja en LaLiga
articles.standfirst: La competición española aventaja ampliamente en expulsiones (23) y promedios a las otras cuatro grandes de Europa; cada jornada se ven casi tres expulsados.
articles.summary: La competición española aventaja ampliamente en expulsiones (23) y promedios a las otras cuatro grandes de Europa; cada jornada se ven casi tres expulsados.
articles.body: Fue expulsado por el siguiente motivo...”. Es una expresión de moda en el fútbol español. LaLiga sufre una avalancha de tarjetas rojas en las primeras curvas del campeonato. El número de expulsiones que se pueden ver en nuestro campos supera ampliamente al de las otras grandes competiciones europeas. Y sólo se llevan ocho jornadas disputadas. Este tramo ha servido para colocar sobre nuestro fútbol un sello de distinción de difícil calibre. En LaLiga ya se han visto 23 expulsiones en ocho jornadas (una media de 2,87 rojas por fecha). No hay rival a la vista. En la Premier y en la Ligue 1 francesa, con 6 jornadas, se han producido 9 expulsiones (media de 1,5). En la Bundesliga después de cinco jornadas se han presenciado cinco expulsiones (una por fecha). En la Serie A italiana, tras seis jornadas, sólo se ha expulsado a cinco futbolistas (0,83). Por partidos disputados, la diferencia también es profunda. En España se han disputado 78 encuentros (el Levante-Athletic y el Rayo-Athletic están pendientes) con una media de 0,29 rojas por partido; en Francia, con 54 partidos, la media es de 0,16; en la Premier, con 60 duelos, se quedan en 0,15, casi la mitad que en LaLiga; en la Bundesliga, con 45 enfrentamientos, el promedio es de 0,11; y en Italia, colista en rojas, la media es de 0,08. El pliego de cargos del gráfico de la parte superior clarifica cómo se expulsa en España: 8 rojas se han enseñado sin intervención del VAR; 5 se han mostrado tras una doble amarilla; 4 se han decidido tras un aviso del VAR y otras seis han sido exhibidas tras una corrección: las tarjetas amarillas quedaron anuladas y se pasaron a la roja tras la petición del VAR. La conclusión es que el VAR ha condicionado más tarjetas rojas que lo visto en el césped por el árbitro de campo. La sala de videoarbitraje ha inducido a diez expulsiones del total de 23. Los colegiados designados para los partidos enseñaron ocho rojas. Deportivo, Getafe, Sevilla y Real Sociedad encabezan, a su pesar, la clasificación de expulsiones sufridas en este trayecto de LaLiga con tres para cada equipo. Con dos figuran Real Madrid y Rayo Vallecano. Con una roja cierran la tabla Celta, Espanyol, Athletic, Elche, Atlético, Racing y Alavés. Entre los equipos sin rojas figuran Barcelona, Betis, Villlarreal o Valencia. Sólo dos de las 23 expulsiones se han producido por protestas o un hecho similar. El rayista Jorge de Frutos fue expulsado en el encuentro disputado en Butarque contra el Racing. El cuadro vallecano recurrió la sanción de dos partidos al alegar que el futbolista había golpeado a una nevera, algo que ni iba en el acta ni se veía en las imágenes. El otro castigado fue Oskarsson, ariete islandés de la Real Sociedad, que ante el Valencia se salió de su perfil habitual, se calentó en un minuto y vio dos amarillas por disconformidad con las decisiones del colegiado, Munuera Montero. Novedosa fue también la manera en la que Isaac Romero se encaminó a los vestuarios en el reciente Levante-Sevilla. El delantero sevillista marcó el 2-3 del encuentro y vio la segunda amarilla por hacer el gesto de silencio sobre una grada, algo que desencadenó un lanzamiento masivo de objetos. Cordero Vega le explicó que fue por el gesto. La tarjeta roja que vio Yuri en el minuto 11 del Athletic-Sevilla tuvo consecuencias. El lateral izquierdo ya había mostrado en el césped su asombro ante la decisión tomada por Soto Grado. El CTA (Comité técnico de árbitros), a través del llamado 'Tiempo de revisión', determinó un “error claro y manifiesto del árbitro de campo. El VAR debió intervenir”. A pesar de ello, Apelación no anuló el castigo al futbolista, que expresó su malestar públicamente.

articles.title: NCAA Sues Ohio Governor Over His Executive Order Allowing Schools to Ignore New Eligibility Rule
articles.summary: The NCAA sued the governor of Ohio on Friday, accusing him of trying to give college athletes in his state a "hall pass" to circumvent a rule that denies players who graduated high school in 2022 from a fifth year of eligibility.
articles.body:
The NCAA sued the governor of Ohio on Friday, accusing him of trying to give college athletes in his state a "hall pass" to circumvent a rule that denies players who graduated high school in 2022 from a fifth year of eligibility.

NCAA President Charlie Baker called the lawsuit, filed in federal court in Ohio, an "extraordinary step" designed to prevent Gov. Mike DeWine from making it "impossible for all schools to compete on a level playing field."

DeWine issued an executive order Tuesday that undercut the NCAA rule, approved over the summer. That and the NCAA's federal lawsuit in reaction to it marks the latest tit-for-tat in a torrent of legal maneuverings that are creating new rules on a state-by-state basis.

"This whole thing has become comical," Danny White, the athletic director at Tennessee, said on social media in reaction to the NCAA announcement.

Under DeWine's order, public and private universities in Ohio would be able to allow the Class of '22 athletes to play, even though the NCAA's new guidance excludes those who have already played four seasons. The rule, passed in June, is the subject of multiple court fights.

In its court filing, the NCAA said it was trying "to halt a misguided attempt to give Ohio colleges and universities an unfair, unprecedented and unwarranted competitive advantage in stadiums and arenas throughout the country,"

"College sports, like all sports, depend on participants following the rules. (DeWine) is attempting to give Ohio institutions a hall pass to break the rules," the lawsuit says.

In reaction to the governor's move, the Ohio Supreme Court said it would step in and determine the legality of the executive order. As part of that, it paused an appeals court ruling in a case there that had declared the '22 athletes ineligible. The court asked both sides to file briefs in the case, in which basketball player Filip Borovićanin is the lead plaintiff, by next Monday.

Baker said the NCAA did not believe the Supreme Court's order did, in fact, declare those players immediately eligible to compete and said it would submit arguments in that case.

That case, like others around the country, is becoming more urgent by the day, as it involves a handful of basketball players whose status for the upcoming season is in jeopardy. Among them: Gonzaga transfer Javon Bennett, Cincinnati's MJ Collins and Borovićanin himself, who played in an exhibition against Tennessee on Thursday night after DeWine's order put him back on the eligible list.

The NCAA has long explained that it knew excluding the Class of '22 from the five-year rule would cause those athletes hardship, but the decision was between them and the new class of high school recruits coming into college this year, many of whom would be displaced if the veterans were allowed another year.

Ultimately, the NCAA made its decision based on which move harmed fewer people.

The NCAA lawsuit goes through the history of the rule and the flood of legal actions that have come since. One of the original cases, a federal lawsuit involving basketball player Brock Wisne, is leaning in the NCAA's direction, though victories there have only spawned more lawsuits in state court.

"The results of this second wave of lawsuits were mixed, with the NCAA winning some and losing others," it said. "But the lawsuits unquestionably destabilized college sports, with ever-more disruptive lawsuits challenging foundational rules at the heart of organized sport."

During testimony in a similar case in Kentucky earlier this week, an NCAA attorney asked Louisville basketball coach Pat Kelsey why he was among those looking for Class of '22 athletes when the NCAA rules forbid that.

"From a coach's standpoint, every time the NCAA says something, we all shrug our shoulders and say, 'Is that going to stand up? Is that a rule?'" Kelsey said. "We don't think there are rules right now. That's why we want guardrails, we want Congress to act, we want the chaos to end. Because nobody knows what the crap is going on. No one."

The NCAA has long called for a federal law to tamp down on the lawsuits undermining its rules for hundreds of thousands of athletes across the country. The Senate has sent the Protect College Sports Act to the House, where its fate is uncertain in this election year.

articles.body: El Betis ha dado a conocer este mediodía la convocatoria para el partido que disputará mañana (18:30 horas) frente al Barcelona en La Cartuja. articles.title: Real Madrid demand Javier Tebas resignation over Joseph Goebbels comparison
articles.summary: Real Madrid have called for the "immediate resignation" of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he compared the club's management to Joseph Goebbels.
articles.body:
Real Madrid have called for the "immediate resignation" of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he drew comparisons between the club's management and Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.

Tebas said Real Madrid's communication and the use of its in-house TV channel "recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels".

Real Madrid have called the statement "deeply offensive" and "morally repugnant".

The club have also demanded Tebas steps down as both the head of the Spanish top flight and vice-president of the Spanish Football Association (RFEF).

"Real Madrid considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone holding two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football resorts to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television," the club said.

In a lengthy post published on X on Friday, Tebas said: "Real Madrid's management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing.

"Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies.

"That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's minister of propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative."

Tebas later said he was drawing comparison with "those propaganda techniques" and "not with an ideology".

Real Madrid rejected this clarification, saying it did not mitigate the "institutionally unworthy nature of his statements".

The club added: "These statements constitute yet another episode in the repeated attacks by Javier Tebas against Real Madrid, its president and its media outlets."

Last month, Tebas criticised Real Madrid for claiming there was a refereeing conspiracy against the club.

He also has been critical of Real and its president Florentino Perez in previous years after disagreeing with their plans to join a European Super League in 2021 .

In 2025 he said Real had "lost their head" after the club sent a formal letter of complaint to the Spanish FA about officiating in the league.

articles.title: Manchester Utd have ‘moved on’ from Martinez outburst, says Carrick
articles.summary: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick says club have ‘moved on’ from Lisandro Martinez blast before Leeds trip.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick said Manchester United had “moved on” from Lisandro Martinez’s outburst aimed at the club’s hierarchy this week, saying it was “really not a drama for us as a group”.

Argentina defender Martinez took aim at the hierarchy of the struggling club following United’s 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, saying Carrick had been left with an under-strength squad.

The centre-back criticised technical director Jason Wilcox , saying he had “100 percent” expected more investment during the summer transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season.

It is understood Martinez has been fined for his outburst, but Carrick said he would be in United’s squad for the Premier League match at Leeds on Sunday.

“It’s done, really,” Carrick said at his pre-match news conference on Friday when asked about Martinez’s comments and his subsequent apology and punishment .

“We’ve moved on from that,” he said. “It was one of those things. He has come out and acknowledged the situation, and as a group we’ve moved on.

“It is really not a drama for us as a group. The boys have trained really well; there was a really good feeling around training this morning.”

Martinez issues apology, but Keane calls Man Utd a ‘circus’

Martinez, 28, issued an apology on Thursday, saying he had held positive talks with the club’s leadership and Carrick.

“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity,” he said in a post on Instagram.

“The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”

Former United captain Roy Keane branded the situation at his former club as “a bit of a circus”.

United travel to Elland Road, the home of one of their fiercest rivals, with just two wins from nine games in all competitions this season.

They are 13th in the Premier League, with just one win from six matches and drew their last match 1-1 against 10-man Tottenham.

articles.title: FC United: The 21-year-old protest club hoping for FA Cup windfall
articles.summary: FC United are hoping for FA Cup success, 21 years after being formed as a supporter-owned club following the Glazer family takeover of Manchester United.
articles.body:
FC United of Manchester striker Adam Le Fondre spent Tuesday lunchtime working with a group of players from the club's academy on a 3G pitch next to the club's 4,900-capacity Broadhurst Park stadium.

The dozen lads are probably not going to get anywhere near the Premier League, as Le Fondre once did, but the Northern Premier League club want to try and create a pathway to senior football, while ensuring the teenagers continue in education through their partnership with Manchester College.

Getting to train with the 39-year-old Le Fondre, scorer of more than 300 goals in professional football including 14 in his sole Premier League season, is the kind of community initiative that goes on at non-league clubs across the country.

For the people who run FC United, it is a world away from the club they once supported.

Just as it is 21 years since the Glazer family bought Manchester United and dropped £600m of debt on the club, it is 21 years since a group of fans decided to stop joining protests against the Americans and instead form their own supporter-owned club.

This weekend, while Michael Carrick takes his team to Leeds, desperate for a win to quieten the noise around him and his club, FC United have a short trip to Altrincham for an FA Cup fourth qualifying round tie that could be worth £25,000.

"We didn't stop loving Manchester United," said chairman Nick Boom. "We started FC United because we loved it.

"Our roots are Manchester United. The songs, the humour, the traditions and shared history still run through FC United.

"But after 21 years, we have also got our own identity. We have a sense of place in North Manchester. We're unmistakably a Manchester club. We have Manchester United fans coming here that have been priced out of Old Trafford. We have fans who feel disassociated with Premier League football.

"We think football, in a sense, has lost its way at the top level. Football should be somewhere you can go with your friends and family, stand or sit together, with a sense of community. Somewhere you can get some decent food and drink at an affordable price, where you can have a beer on the terraces, have a sing-song and forget your troubles for a couple of hours.

"Fewer people are able to do that at the very top level, on the grounds of affordability and accessibility. We believe we're more important than ever with everything that's going on at the moment."

FC United distribute a monthly board meeting summary to their 1,528 adult members which explains the minutiae of club operations.

The solar power generation at Broadhurst Park is going to be increased, which the club think will save up to £4,000. A £5,000 donation has been received from one fan and there was also an update on the 'own your own football club for £5-a-month initiative' and comparisons made with other supporter-owned clubs, including Bury, whose relaunch has taken them into the same league as FC United.

The pair meet on Boxing Day in a game likely to attract a huge attendance at Broadhurst Park.

Yet, like Manchester United, FC United has a significant debt.

"Supporter ownership isn't easy," said Boom. "There's no billionaire ready to write a cheque at the end of the month to make up any shortfalls.

"The debt did get out of control for a period. It absolutely did, because the clamour was to have our own ground; somewhere we could truly call home.

"But we overextended and the ground wasn't as well managed as it could have been. We've learned some harsh lessons from that about the level of expertise you need, even at a club at this level, to run it."

Members still don't want FC United to have a front of shirt sponsor but naming rights for the stadium which 'is showing wear and tear', is being discussed.

A recent change of personnel at senior level has led to a 'review of the club's relationships' with existing commercial backers. The club pride themselves on linking up with local and independent businesses when they can.

Boom's employment background is in finance. He is trying to ensure the financial side of the club is in order.

A profit in excess of £100,000 is forecast for the current year, a £350,000 improvement. But it is felt an annual surplus of £200,000 is needed to ensure funds can be found for essential work on and around the ground, as well as to allow the club to meet its loan repayments.

He estimates he spends 70 hours a week on club business, not bad for a volunteer who lives in West Yorkshire.

You can tell he loves it though. Whereas once Boom watched Manchester United win Premier Leagues, FA Cups and European trophies, now he is looking forward to a trip to Altrincham, currently in the National League play-off places.

The winners pocket £9,375 and would be guaranteed at least another £15,800 in prize money by reaching the first round. The loser gets £3,125. That money is important, although Boom says once the whistle blows, his focus will be on football not finance.

Twenty-four hours later, Manchester United head to Leeds, the next stop in a season of turmoil, which has triggered the type of fierce protests he was once a part of but now observes, even if a close relationship has developed with the 1958 Group, who have been at the forefront of recent protests.

"What has happened to Manchester United is an absolute tragedy," he said.

"This is one of the world's great sporting institutions, a football club with an extraordinary history, built on the achievements, sacrifices and loyalty of generations of people.

"Yet for more than 20 years it's been treated increasingly as a financial asset by owners who appear completely disconnected from what the club means to its supporters.

"The Glazers' ownership has been disgraceful. They acquired Manchester United through a leveraged takeover, burdened it with debt and have benefited enormously from something they did nothing to create. Meanwhile, the club has suffered years of decline and its relationship with supporters has been steadily eroded.

"I see very little evidence that Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS represent a fundamentally different philosophy. Ratcliffe might talk about restoring Manchester United but you cannot rebuild a football club by dismantling the very culture and community that made it great."

Ratcliffe has implemented a number of controversial measures since agreeing a minority stake in United in December 2023, including two lots of redundancies. He has defended the action, saying it was essential to return the club to profitability.

"We have enormous respect for anyone continuing to protest," added Boom. "It was particularly pleasing that, after more than 20 years, The 1958 Group reached out to FC United.

"We've developed a good relationship, and while we've taken different paths, we're united by a belief that Manchester United and its supporters deserve better."

articles.title: Hamza refuerza el filial
articles.standfirst: El egipcio jugará esta jornada con el Barça Atlètic contra el Utebo
articles.summary: El egipcio jugará esta jornada con el Barça Atlètic contra el Utebo
articles.body: Hamza fue la principal ausencia en la expedición culé que este viernes viajó a Sevilla para enfrentarse mañana sábado al Betis. De hecho, el delantero egipcio ya no se ejercitó esta tarde con el primer equipo. Los técnicos decidieron que esta jornada refuerce al Barça Atlètic en su compromiso contra el Utebo. El delantero no estaba teniendo protagonismo en este arranque de temporada. Solo ha disputado doce minutos en total entre LaLiga y la Champions, una cifra muy baja para un jugador tan joven. Por ello, esta jornada jugará con el filial. Además, el propio Hamza ya dijo durante la rueda de prensa de su renovación que no le importaría bajar al B si los técnicos lo considerasen oportuno. El gran rendimiento de Raphinha como falso nueve, que además ya está de vuelta con el equipo tras perderse dos partidos por un edema, los buenos minutos de Gabriel Jesus y el hecho de que Flick incluso probara a Olmo en esa posición contra el Galatasaray cierran prácticamente la puerta al internacional egipcio. De momento, Hamza jugará con el filial, aunque habrá que ver si se trata de una decisión puntual o permanente.

articles.title: Real Madrid demand resignation of La Liga chief after Goebbels comparison
articles.summary: La Liga President Javier Tebas under fire for comparing Real Madrid TV channel to Nazi Germany’s Minister of Propaganda.
articles.body:
Real Madrid are demanding the ‌‌resignation of La Liga President Javier Tebas after he compared rhetoric from ⁠⁠the club’s management ⁠⁠to the propaganda methods used by the Nazi Party in Germany.

Tebas wrote earlier on Friday on social media that “Real Madrid’s management directs an orchestra of ⁠⁠mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing”.

The LaLiga president was responding to articles by two journalists saying he and LaLiga were acting against Real’s interests.

Tebas added that the authors ⁠⁠in El Debate newspaper were amplifying a message on behalf of Real’s management.

Real Madrid’s demand for Tebas to immediately resign deepens a feud between the club and La Liga’s chief.

Last month, Real called for a new LaLiga president in response ‌‌to Tebas calling their complaints about refereeing decisions ‘a smokescreen’ for their shortcomings on the pitch.

Tebas on Friday criticised Real Madrid TV’s coverage of officiating at their matches.

“Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion and point fingers at the enemies,” he wrote.

“That method recalls propaganda mechanisms used by Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s Minister of Propaganda.

“The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with ⁠⁠an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase,” added ⁠⁠LaLiga’s president.

Real Madrid demand Tebas’s resignation as La Liga chief

Real Madrid released a statement later on Friday demanding that Tebas resign from his positions as LaLiga chief and vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation.

The statement called it “intolerable and extraordinarily serious” that ⁠⁠Tebas used “a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television.

“Tebas’ repeated conduct ⁠⁠demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with ⁠⁠his institutional responsibilities,” said Real.

“It is unacceptable that he even takes advantage of questions, information or opinions from journalists unrelated to the club to direct his accusations at us, attributing to us actions of third parties for which ‌‌we bear no responsibility.”

The 64-year-old, who is elected by the 42 professional clubs in Spain’s top two tiers, has been La Liga president since 2013. In 2023, he was ‌‌re-elected ‌‌unopposed until 2027.

Real Madrid’s statement came hours after La Liga confirmed that they are one of the six clubs that will sit on the league’s Executive Committee this season.

articles.title: Iñigo Pérez: “No pienso en Liverpool y espero que los jugadores tampoco”
articles.standfirst: El técnico espera que la plantilla aparque la Champions para centrarse en La Liga
articles.summary: El técnico espera que la plantilla aparque la Champions para centrarse en La Liga
articles.body: El Villarreal afronta el partido ante el Elche en mitad de dos partidos tan atractivos como el del Nápoles y el del Liverpool. Es por ello que Iñigo exige a la plantilla máxima atención en el duelo ante los ilicitanos donde pueden consolidar su recuperación en Liga. Cómo afrontan el partido: "A priori estamos bien todos, no tenemos ningún inconveniente respecto al último partido. Esperamos seguir así.Ver la carga muscular y tomar decisiones. Viendo la plantilla que tengo no es posible que sea alguien encorsetado". Sobre Gulacsi: "Peter está bien, está con nosotros. Al siguiente día se incorporó. Es una persona con una gran fuerza mental. No es sencillo, pero ha decidido que lo mejor para pasar este mal trago es volver a los entrenamientos. Le veo bien, mañana decidimos”. Elogios de de Anselmi: "Agradezco sus palabras. Nos conocimos el año pasado y fue productivo para los dos. Él tiene más experiencia que yo, ha estado en grandes equipos. Es bueno para la Liga que esté aquí. Y si nos centramos en su Elche vemos cosas importantes a nivel físico, de ideas, de situaciones que tenemos que tener en cuenta para mañana. Si vemos cómo se han desarrollado sus partidos, sabemos de la dificultad del rival". Esfuerzos de Renato Veiga: "En el caso de Renato tiene una tolerancia muy buena a los partidos y esfuerzos continuados. La jerarquía y el nivel que muestra y la posición que ocupa hacen que le mantengan de forma continuada en el once, pero sabemos que tenemos que cuidar de los jugadores. Él se encuentra bien, responde bien". Jornada entre dos partidos Champions: “Siempre ocurre que hay un partido que socialmente es el deseado. Todo el mundo piensa en el Liverpool, pero yo no y los jugadores espero que tampoco. La única forma es hacerles ver que si mañana pierdes, ¿cómo viajas a Liverpool? Direccionarse para que se den cuenta que no es otro partido que el de mañana. Tenemos que centrarnos en ir a ganar con solvencia porque somos el Villarreal”. El Elche a domicilio: “Es un equipo muy fuerte físicamente, juegan muy bien, tienen una personalidad que han heredado, unas propuestas familiares y que los jugadores están coordinados, eso les hace un equipo difícil. Liverpool ojalá sea muy bonito pero no entiendo otra forma de mirar el partido de mañana”. Si ganan se posicionan bien: “Mañana es un momento perfecto para seguir desarrollando las virtudes que venimos viendo, equilibrarnos en la clasificación y equilibrarnos como equipo después de un comienzo que nos ha pillado un poco a traspiés”.

articles.title: From Cristiano Ronaldo to Ronaldinho: how these 10 football stars earned UAE Golden Visas and made Emirates second home for business and beyond
articles.summary: Explore how top football stars like Cristiano Ronaldo and Ronaldinho have embraced the UAE Golden Visa, establishing businesses, mentoring young talent, and connecting to the region's vibrant sports landscape.
articles.body: The UAE has spent years attracting some of football’s biggest names, but its Golden Visa programme offers more than a convenient way for global stars to visit the Emirates. Since the government expanded eligibility to exceptional sporting talent in 2020, footballers have used their connections with the country in different ways, from establishing businesses and investing in local football to building media ventures and developing opportunities for young players. Here are 10 footballers who received the coveted residency, and what their relationships with the UAE have looked like beyond the initial announcements.What is the UAE Golden Visa, and why did footballers become eligible?The UAE introduced its Golden Residency programme in 2019 under an initiative announced by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the country’s Vice-President and Prime Minister and Dubai’s ruler. Initially associated with investors, entrepreneurs and specialised professionals, the programme offered eligible foreign nationals a longer-term alternative to conventional residence permits tied to employment or local sponsorship.A significant expansion followed in 2020, when the UAE Cabinet extended the 10-year residency pathway to exceptional sporting talent. The Dubai Sports Council helped bring prominent international athletes into the programme, with Cristiano Ronaldo and several other football stars forming part of the first sporting cohort.The change reflected an ambition extending beyond attracting famous visitors. Under the UAE’s economic diversification strategy, including the longer-term objectives associated with We the UAE 2031 and Dubai’s D33 Economic Agenda, global talent can help strengthen industries beyond oil, including technology, tourism, healthcare, education and professional sport.Footballers offer a particularly visible connection between those ambitions and the wider public. Their international audiences can bring attention to local sporting facilities, youth development programmes, commercial partnerships and investment opportunities, while some recipients have gone on to establish more direct professional or business ties with the country.What does the Golden Visa offer, and who can qualify?The Golden Visa is a renewable, long-term residency permit that allows eligible foreign nationals to live, work, study and invest in the UAE without requiring an employer or another local sponsor to maintain their residency. Depending on the applicable category and eligibility conditions, the permit can last five or 10 years.Its main benefits include:Long-term residency: Eligible holders receive renewable residency, providing greater continuity than shorter-term permits.Family sponsorship: Holders can sponsor spouses, children regardless of age and parents, alongside domestic workers under applicable regulations.Greater travel flexibility: Golden Visa holders can remain outside the UAE beyond the usual six-month absence limit that applies to many other residence visas.Professional independence: The residency arrangement does not depend on maintaining a conventional local employer sponsorship.Work, study and investment: Holders can pursue eligible professional, educational and commercial activities within the UAE.Entry arrangements for overseas applicants: Eligible applicants outside the country may receive a six-month multiple-entry visa, renewable for another six months, to complete residency procedures.Following the expansion, the programme now covers several categories, including property investors, entrepreneurs, scientists, skilled professionals, outstanding students and graduates, humanitarian pioneers, and exceptional talents in sport, culture and the arts. Each pathway has its own criteria and application or nomination process, so receiving the visa does not necessarily require buying property or taking up employment with a UAE-based organisation.For footballers, the expanded sporting category created a route to long-term residency based on exceptional achievement and talent, rather than requiring them to leave their existing clubs and move to the Emirates.Ten footballers who received the UAE Golden Visa1. Cristiano Ronaldo (February 2020)Portuguese forward Cristiano Ronaldo received his 10-year UAE Golden Visa in February 2020 while playing for Juventus, becoming one of the most prominent beneficiaries of the newly expanded sporting category. The recognition followed his sixth Best Men's Player accolade at the Dubai Globe Soccer Awards on 29 December 2019, reflecting both his international standing and his established relationship with the Emirate.His placement in the inaugural sporting cohort demonstrated that an athlete could maintain an active career abroad while holding long-term UAE residency. Ronaldo subsequently signed with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia in January 2023, extending his commitment through June 2027, while frequently visiting Dubai for personal and professional obligations. To anchor this long-term connection to the region, Ronaldo expanded his international real estate portfolio by acquiring a €25 million plot of land on Jumeirah Bay Island—a highly exclusive, seahorse-shaped enclave widely known as "Billionaire Island". The acquisition was made to construct a custom waterfront mega-mansion, providing a permanent family base in the UAE just a short distance from his football commitments in Riyadh.His relationship with the Emirates also features a prominent personal dimension, highlighted by a well-documented friendship with the Crown Prince of Dubai, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum. Ronaldo has repeatedly spoken warmly of the city, stating during an appearance at Expo 2020 Dubai on 28 January 2022: “I thank all my fans... I love Dubai, its culture and its people, and I visit Dubai every year, and I am very happy to be here.”2. Didier Drogba (November 2020)Former Chelsea and Ivory Coast striker Didier Drogba received his Golden Visa in November 2020, when Major General Mohammad Ahmad Al Marri, director of Dubai’s General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs, welcomed him at the department’s headquarters to present the residency card.The recognition came after a decorated career that included four English Premier League titles and a Champions League crown with Chelsea. Drogba was also presented with the Medal of First Line of Defence in appreciation of his support for the Dubai Sports Council’s Be Fit, Be Safe campaign, which encouraged residents to prioritise physical wellbeing during the pandemic.His connection with Dubai extended beyond football, with the former striker exploring opportunities involving commercial property, sports academies and the wider sports sector. He has also participated in international business events, including AIBC Eurasia, bringing his sporting profile into discussions around emerging technology, blockchain and investment.3. Ronaldinho (May 2021)Brazilian World Cup winner Ronaldinho, whose full name is Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, received his 10-year Golden Visa in May 2021 through Dubai’s General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs. Major General Mohammed Al Marri and his deputy, Major General Obaid Muhair bin Surour, were present when the former Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker received the residency.Ronaldinho’s relationship with the UAE has included ambitions around youth football and wider sporting partnerships. He signed a strategic memorandum of understanding with Abu Dhabi-based Palms Sports, establishing a framework intended to combine elite athletic development with academic opportunities for young Emirati athletes.He has also laid the groundwork for a Ronaldinho Football Academy in Dubai, with the proposed project centred on structured coaching and the Brazilian approach to attacking football commonly associated with Joga Bonito. His wider appearances across the region have included sports events, corporate gatherings and digital-technology exhibitions, where his global profile attracts audiences beyond traditional football supporters.Ronaldinho has regularly visited and trained in Dubai since his youth, making the city a familiar base for his regional engagements. His Golden Visa provides long-term residency flexibility while he explores sporting, commercial and cultural opportunities across the Emirates.4. Paul Pogba (February 2020)French midfielder and World Cup winner Paul Pogba was among the elite sporting figures granted a UAE Golden Visa in February 2020. At the time, the former Manchester United star had already established a strong connection with Dubai, regularly utilizing the city's sports infrastructure for off-season conditioning and warm-weather training.Dubai’s high-performance training centres have been central to Pogba’s conditioning and rehabilitation, particularly at Nad Al Sheba Sports Complex and Transform Altitude Performance Center. He has also supported local fitness campaigns with the Dubai Sports Council and mentored young players at community events.His regional interests have since expanded beyond football into traditional Gulf sports culture. In late 2025, Pogba became a significant shareholder and global ambassador for Al Haboob, the world’s first professional camel racing team. The Saudi-founded organization competes heavily across the UAE and the wider Gulf region, aiming to modernize the sport by introducing advanced sports science, data tracking, and robotic jockey technology. Pogba’s involvement is intended to help elevate camel racing to a global audience, bridging the gap between historical heritage and modern professional sports management.5. Romelu Lukaku (February 2020)Belgian striker Romelu Lukaku was another big name from that initial wave of sports stars to secure a UAE Golden Visa in February 2020, right while he was dominating Serie A with Inter Milan. The long-term residency was a massive nod to his status as one of Europe’s top forwards, giving him a permanent tie to the Emirates without having to uproot his club career.Lukaku’s Dubai connection grew at the 14th Dubai International Sports Conference, where he joined João Félix and Mikael Silvestre to discuss football technology. He also spoke about coping with online racism, urging young players to use social media positively. The event ended with a viral moment when a UAE royal presented him with a golden plaque that misspelled his name as “Romello”.When he isn’t speaking at summits, Lukaku uses Dubai as his ultimate reset button. He’s a regular at the world-class Nad Al Sheba Sports Complex during league winter breaks, using the warm weather and high-tech facilities to keep his conditioning at an elite level. His routine fits perfectly into Dubai's push to become the global capital for off-season athletic recovery.6. Luís Figo (February 2020)Former Portugal international Luís Figo, the 2000 Ballon d’Or winner who played for Barcelona, Real Madrid and Inter Milan, received his Golden Visa as part of the February 2020 sporting initiative. The residency recognised his career at the highest level while giving him a long-term base for professional and commercial activities across the region.Figo has maintained links with Dubai through brand partnerships and sporting events, including collaborations with Mastercard Middle East and Africa during Expo 2020 Dubai. His appearances included fan meet-and-greet sessions and promotional activities featuring the UEFA Champions League trophy.He also participated in a Guinness World Record initiative involving the highest-altitude football match played on a parabolic flight, a campaign coordinated through Dubai. Alongside those commercial engagements, Figo supported the Dubai Sports Council’s Be Fit, Be Safe campaign during the pandemic, encouraging residents to remain physically active while public spaces were restricted.His post-playing career has increasingly involved ambassadorial work and international business events, making the Golden Visa a useful foundation for maintaining commitments across Europe and the Middle East.7. Roberto Carlos (February 2020)Brazilian World Cup winner and former Real Madrid left-back Roberto Carlos received his Golden Visa in February 2020, joining a group of football legends recognised for their sporting achievements and connections with the Emirates. His relationship with Dubai has included exhibition matches, community fitness initiatives and youth football development.In August 2026, Carlos became a co-owner and shareholder of Dubai-based Fursan Hispania FC, alongside former footballers Michel Salgado and Fernando Hierro. The club’s youth development ambitions offer him a more direct role in the local game, using international football connections and technical experience to help develop young players and create pathways towards professional opportunities in Europe.Carlos has also supported the Real Madrid Foundation’s work in the UAE through a partnership with ISD Sports City, helping launch an educational football programme at the ISD La Liga Academy campus. The initiative provides training for more than 1,000 young footballers.His work also includes youth clinics and appearances promoting Real Madrid World at Dubai Parks and Resorts, extending his involvement from football development into the UAE’s sports tourism sector.8. Miralem Pjanić (February 2020)Bosnian midfielder Miralem Pjanić received his Golden Visa in February 2020 while playing for Juventus, becoming one of the active European footballers included in the programme’s first sporting cohort. His subsequent career gave him a particularly direct connection with the Emirates when he left Barcelona in September 2022 to join Sharjah FC.Unlike recipients whose UAE relationships have centred mainly on visits and commercial appearances, Pjanić played in the UAE Pro League for two seasons between 2022 and 2024. His experience at Juventus and Barcelona brought elite European experience into the domestic competition, and he helped Sharjah win the UAE President’s Cup and the UAE League Cup.During his time in the country, Pjanić also had opportunities to mentor younger domestic players, sharing experience from years competing at the highest levels of European football. Following his UAE spell and later playing career, he maintained ties with Dubai and became involved with Mundial Football Academy, a venture focused on identifying and training grassroots talent using high-performance football methods.9. Rio Ferdinand (2021)Former Manchester United and England captain Rio Ferdinand transitioned to a permanent life in the UAE in August 2025, relocating his family to a £6.5 million mansion in Dubai's luxury Al Barari community. This move followed his departure from his prominent UK punditry role at TNT Sports in May 2025. While he enjoyed a long-standing relationship with the region, this relocation marked the formal establishment of Dubai as the central base for his media work, business interests, and 10-year UAE Golden Visa residency framework.Ferdinand has since actively scaled his digital media platform, Rio Presents, while anchoring himself in the UAE’s expanding creator economy. He was featured as a prominent fireside speaker at Dubai’s 1 Billion Followers Summit, where he discussed the future of digital media and how modern creators can build sustainable international audiences independently of traditional television.Beyond media, his regional business activities extend into real estate through strategic partnerships with prominent firms like LEOS Developments. In the sports and tourism sector, he co-operates Football Escapes, a premium holiday football coaching concept that organizes youth camps led by UEFA-licensed former professionals at luxury resorts.Ferdinand and his wife, Kate, also engage with the local community through public wellness initiatives, including fitness events hosted at Jumeirah Beach near the Burj Al Arab.10. Patrice Evra (2021)Former Manchester United champion and French national team captain Patrice Evra was awarded his UAE Golden Visa back in 2021 under the exceptional-talent framework. . Since then, he has fully leaned into the local lifestyle, famously calling Dubai his "home sweet home" and basing himself out of a luxury penthouse on the Palm Jumeirah.Instead of just enjoying retirement, Evra has used his long-term visa to pivot into a serious second career as a Dubai-based entrepreneur. He has set up several companies in the UAE covering everything from beauty and fitness to deep tech. In fact, while speaking at regional business events like the Invest in Sharjah forum and Token2049 Dubai, he pointed out just how much of a game-changer the region's geography is for a global business. He noted that with nearly two-thirds of the world’s population sitting within an eight-hour flight, running a global empire from Dubai feels a world away from his old days managing companies in the UK, where he felt entirely isolated from fast-growing markets like Asia.Lately, Evra has been bridging the gap between real estate and sports technology. He officially partnered with UAE developer Major Developments as a core project partner for Colibri Views, a massive new high-rise project at RAK Central in Ras Al Khaimah. Evra actually designed the crown jewel of the tower himself: the UAE's very first rooftop Footbot simulator. It’s an AI-driven, high-tech football arena packed with smart motion sensors and performance tracking to help residents train like elite pros.On top of the commercial tech, he is also focused on grassroots football through his Dubai-based project, Love This Game FC. The whole idea is to scout and train young local talent in the UAE, giving them a real pathway to score professional trials over in Europe and the UK.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Watch: Barcelona star put through tunnel of slaps in training
articles.summary: Barcelona star Raphinha was the latest member of Hansi Flick’s squad put through a traditional ‘tunnel of slaps’ during training on Friday.This came after th...
articles.body:
Barcelona star Raphinha was the latest member of Hansi Flick's squad put through a traditional 'tunnel of slaps' during training on Friday.

This came after the Brazilian was given the green light to rejoin full group activities alongside the rest of his teammates at the Ciutat Esportiva.

Frontman Raphinha was for his part forced to sit out each of Barcelona's last two fixtures, against Getafe and Galatasaray respectively, owing to a muscular issue suffered whilst on international duty with Brazil last month.

The former Leeds United man spent recent days ramping up his recovery under the watch of the Blaugrana's medical staff, with a view to being available to play his part against Real Betis this weekend.

And as alluded to above, after being cleared for full contact drills on Friday morning, Raphinha's comeback was marked by a traditional process in Catalunya's capital.

As proves the case upon any Barca player returning to fitness, the 29-year-old was subjected to a 'tunnel of slaps' courtesy of his teammates:
